key_insight: IVA uses a locally deployed small language model for case-level genomic interpretation, recovering 93% of expert-reported causative variants in 327 solved singleton cases.
clinical_relevance: Local deployment could support privacy-preserving genomic interpretation, but low precision underscores the need for expert review.
method: Benchmarked 13 small language models on 150 genetics questions and selected Qwen3.5-9B.
Used a four-stage pipeline for ACMG/AMP criteria assignment, trio inheritance reasoning, and structured reporting.
Assigned retrieval, phasing, point summation, citation checking, and formatting to deterministic code.
evidence_signal: Evaluated on synthetic scenarios, 16 solved trios, and 327 solved visual-impairment singleton cases; reported trio sensitivity was 100% with 39.5% precision, and singleton recovery was 93% with 43% precision.
watch_item: Evaluation on solved cases does not establish prospective clinical reliability; omissions, unverified mechanisms, reasoning–label mismatches, and arithmetic errors remained.
paper_title: IVA, a locally deployable Intelligent Variant Analyser based on a small language model for complete case-level and trio-based genomic interpretation.
